reuse.why: The API reuses getScheduledAmount and approximate planning reuses getApproxNumberThreshold, but several consumers retain dispatch logic already handled by the shared amount helpers.

duplication.why: Three consumers retain repeated missing/number/range dispatch, and the budget template separately selects which operators reach the shared planning definition.

placement.why: Planning policy belongs in shared/schedules, tolerance remains in shared/rules, and API serialization stays in api-models.

scope.why: All edits concern schedule amount planning, its API exposure, tests, or release notes.

maintainability.why: Overlapping amount helpers, caller-owned policy dispatch, optional operator propagation, and contradictory documentation make future rule changes difficult to apply consistently.

bypasses_abstraction.where: updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule, and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions handle numeric and missing amounts locally instead of delegating the complete decision; createScheduleList also gates getPlannedAmount by operator.

disguised_duplication.where: The three missing/number/range ternaries replace only their range arithmetic with getPlannedAmount, preserving duplicated dispatch around an apparently shared implementation.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains an optional op parameter, getPlannedAmount adds an isapprox branch, and four consumers retain local dispatch around the shared policy.
